newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 1996 net farm income seen at $51 billion-USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 1996 net farm income seen at $51 billion-USDA.

text.p: USDA Friday forecast net farm income would be $51 billion in 1996, a substantial increase from the $43 billion averaged in the past five years.
Net cash income for farms would be $58 billion, up from an average $53 billion, USDA said in a report.
Strong crop receipts, which are expected to be a record, were a major reason for the expected higher income. Tight grain supplies kept grain prices high, and production was also high.
Vegetable fruit and greenhouse receipts should continue their steady growth, the Agricultural Income and Finance summary said.
Overall, livestock receipts were expected to be up, led by hogs, poultry and dairy products. Cattle receipts for 1996 could be the lowest so far in the 1990s, USDA said.
